# Introduction

The **mixggm** package implements mixtures of Gaussian graphical models for model-based clustering with sparse covariance and concentration matrices. 
Estimation of a mixture of Gaussian covariance or concentration graph models using structural-EM algorithm. The mixture model selected is the optimal model according to BIC.

This document gives a quick tour of **mixggm** (version `r packageVersion("mixggm")`) functionalities. It was written in [Quarto](https://quarto.org), using the [knitr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=knitr) package to execute R code. 
See `help(package="mixggm")` for further details and references provided by `citation("mixggm")`.

```{r}
#| label: load-mixggm
#| echo: !expr 1
#| message: false
library(mixggm)
cat(mixggm:::mixggmStartupMessage(), sep="")
```

# Fit a mixture of concentration graph models

## Iris data

```{r}
#| label: iris-fit
data(iris)
mod = mixGGM(iris[,-5], model = "concentration")
summary(mod)
summary(mod, graphs = TRUE, clusters = TRUE, parameters = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: iris-graph
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
plot(mod, what = "graph")
```

```{r}
#| label: iris-adjacency
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "80%"
plot(mod, what = "adjacency")
```

```{r}
#| label: iris-classification
plot(mod, what = "classification")
```

```{r}
#| label: iris-common
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "80%"
plot(mod, what = "common")
```

## A complex simulated data example

```{r}
#| label: complex-simulation
#| echo: !expr -1
set.seed(20190105)
N = 500
V = 20
tau = c(0.3, 0.7)
Nk = rowSums( rmultinom(N, 1, tau) )
class = rep(1:2, Nk)
sigma1 = rWishart(1, V+1, diag(V))[,,1]
mu1 = rep(0, V)
mu2 = rnorm(V, 0.5, 2)
x1 = MASS::mvrnorm(Nk[1], mu1, sigma1)
x2 = matrix(NA, Nk[2], V)
x2[,1] = rnorm(Nk[2])
for(j in 2:V) 
  x2[,j] = x2[,j-1] + rnorm(Nk[2], mu2[j], sd = 0.5)
x = rbind(x1, x2)
colnames(x) = paste0("x", 1:ncol(x))
```

```{r}
#| label: complex-fit
#| echo: !expr 1:2
#| eval: false
mod = mixGGM(x, K = 1:4, model = "concentration",
              penalty = "ebic", beta = 0.5)
if(!file.exists("simcomplex.Rdata"))
  save(mod, file = "simcomplex.Rdata")
```

```{r}
#| label: complex-summary
#| echo: !expr -1
load(file = "simcomplex.Rdata")
summary(mod)
```

```{r}
#| label: complex-classification
plot(mod, what = "classification", dimens = c(1,5,10,15,20))
```

```{r}
#| label: complex-graph
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
plot(mod, what = "graph")
```

```{r}
#| label: complex-adjacency
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "80%"
plot(mod, what = "adjacency")
table(class, mod$classification)
```

# Fit a mixture of covariance graph models

## Wine data

```{r}
#| label: wine-data
data(wine, package = "gclus")
```

```{r}
#| label: wine-fit
#| echo: !expr 1:2
#| eval: false
mod = mixGGM(wine[,-1], K = 1:4, model = "covariance",
             penalty = "erdos", beta = 0.01)
if(!file.exists("wine.Rdata")) 
  save(mod, file = "wine.Rdata")
```

```{r}
#| label: wine-summary
#| echo: !expr -1
load(file = "wine.Rdata")
summary(mod, graphs = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: wine-graph
plot(mod, what = "graph")
```

```{r}
#| label: wine-adjacency
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "80%"
plot(mod, what = "adjacency")
```

```{r}
#| label: wine-classification
plot(mod, what = "classification", dimens = 1:4)
table(wine$Class, mod$classification)
mclust::adjustedRandIndex(wine$Class, mod$classification)
```

## A simple simulated data example

```{r}
#| label: simple-simulation
#| echo: !expr -1
set.seed(20190105)
N = 200
tau = c(0.3, 0.7)
Nk = rowSums( rmultinom(N, 1, tau) )
class = rep(1:2, Nk)
sigma1 = diag(2)                          # independent variables
sigma2 = matrix( c(1,0.9,0.9,1), 2,2 )    # correlated variables
mu1 = c(0, 0)
mu2 = c(2, 3)
x = rbind(MASS::mvrnorm(Nk[1], mu1, sigma1),
           MASS::mvrnorm(Nk[2], mu2, sigma2))
colnames(x) = paste0("x", 1:ncol(x))
mod = mixGGM(x, model = "covariance")
summary(mod, graphs = TRUE, parameters = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: simple-graph
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "80%"
plot(mod, what = "graph")
```

```{r}
#| label: simple-adjacency
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "80%"
plot(mod, what = "adjacency")
```

```{r}
#| label: simple-classification
#| out-width: "80%"
plot(mod, what = "classification")
```
